issues.description: Method name mismatch for the Pneumatic interface: the UML in the problem statement declares an abstract method openValve() (problem_statement.md lines 16-19), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares void releaseValve() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 7). The concrete classes in the solution (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement a method named openValve() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedDropdownTower.java line 15 and solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedRollerCoaster.java line 15). This inconsistent identifier naming between the interface and its implementations will cause a compilation error and confuses students which method name they are supposed to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix to match the UML and tests: rename the method in the solution's Pneumatic interface from releaseValve() to openValve(), and keep the existing openValve() implementations in LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster. Alternatively, if releaseValve() is intended, update the UML/problem statement (and any tests) to use releaseValve() and rename the implementing methods accordingly. Ensure the interface and all implementing classes use the exact same method name and signature.
